text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Delhi's ambassador to Vietnam said his government was preparing for an official visit by Vietnamese Prime Minister, Vo Van Kiet, to India.
-- The Vietnam War Veterans' Association has become the seventh full member of the Veterans' Confederation of ASEAN Countries (VECONAC).
-- The Communications and Transport Consulting and Designing Corporation (Tedi) will begin drafting a feasibility study for the construction of a new north-south highway.
-- By the end of February, Vietnam will have disbursed more than $350 million from total overseas loans of $800 million made in 1996, a Ministry of Finance report showed.
-- South Korea's Daewoo and Posco groups have chosen Quang Ninh province for their investment in a huge steel plant venture with Vietnam Steel Corporation.

-- State Bank of Vietnam Governor Cao Si Kiem has issued a circular reconfirming that local commercial banks will not be allowed to provide credit valued at more than 10 percent of their total capital and reserves without his permission.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi told Seoul's ambassador to Vietnam that he hoped South Korean investors would strengthen their cooperation and business in Vietnam.
-- Russia's visiting Duma Speaker Gennady Seleznyov left Hanoi for Ho Chi Minh City on Tuesday.

-- Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai has called on the Vietnam War Veterans' Association to make greater contributions to heightening public vigilance against "peaceful evolution" and subversive plots of hostile forces.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's party committee has ordered further investigations into the Tamexco corruption case.
-- A three-day meeting of the ASEAN Consultative Committee on Standards and Quality began in Ho Chi Minh City on Monday.
